# Transcript Analysis

## Flow and Ownership

[`parseClaudeSession()`](mex://function:0efb013f713a5e702da7fe74750295d3) turns Claude Code JSONL into a core `Session`: it preserves tree messages and lineage, deduplicates provider usage by message id, stitches tool uses to later results, lifts file and memory operations, builds turns, and records compaction hints and parse warnings.

[`reconstructContext()`](mex://function:80836b3aa8e46550bf1c4ecf6d64de86) projects the session through a message cutoff into attributed segments. History text is counted with the injected `TokenCounter`; file and tool-result sizes reuse adapter counts so content is not double-counted. Every emitted status is initially `unknown`.

[`analyzeSessionReclaimable()`](mex://function:68ee84f89f124bc8ff02912759663751) composes reconstruction, session-aware classification, and report folding. Classification proves duplicates by content hash, superseded copies by file-op order, gone/drifted files through `RepoState`, and marks older one-shot/MCP outputs as heuristic `spent`.

Cost accounting is a sibling analysis: provider usage is priced per message; unknown models remain explicitly unpriced. Reclaimable recurring cost uses the model's cache-read rate.

## Invariants

- Keep raw Claude Code field shapes in the adapter; analysis consumes only core types.
- A `tool_result` user event is not a new user prompt. Multi-line assistant responses can repeat usage but must be billed once per provider message id.
- File-tool output is represented as file content, while non-file results become `tool_result`/`mcp` segments; do not count the same bytes twice.
- Snapshot totals cover attributed transcript content only. System prompts and tool definitions are unavailable and intentionally excluded from the denominator.
- `gone`, `stale-drift`, `stale-superseded`, and `duplicate` are provable; `spent-tool` and `spent-mcp` are heuristic and must remain distinguishable.
- The current reconstruction is linear over `messages`; sidechains remain in the model but are not isolated into separate subagent windows.

## Tests and Fixtures

- Parser changes belong beside `packages/adapter-claude-code/src/parse.test.ts`; extend the anonymized JSONL fixture when a raw schema case must survive end-to-end normalization.
- Analysis changes belong in co-located tests such as `packages/analysis/src/context.test.ts` and reclaimable/cost tests. Inject deterministic token counters and fake `RepoState` implementations.
- Protect malformed-line warnings, usage deduplication, tool pairing, turn boundaries, memory inference, file timestamps, duplicate order, and last-turn `spent` exclusions.

## Known Limits

- The CLI's `EstimateTokenCounter` is approximately four characters per token; only provider usage cost is exact.
- Pricing is a dated local table; unfamiliar model identifiers produce `null` cost rather than a guess.
- Claude Code is the only concrete adapter today.
